claims.text: Grain storage protects harvested grains such as wheat, corn and rice from environmental elements and biological deterioration over extended periods.
claims.label: protecting wheat, corn and rice

claims.text: Traditional storage used simple methods such as stacking bins, while modern systems use sophisticated technology to reduce losses.
claims.label: the shift from stacking bins

claims.text: Temperature control is paramount because elevated temperatures accelerate enzymatic reactions and microbial growth, leading to rancidity, mold and nutrient degradation.
claims.label: heat driving spoilage

claims.text: Most commercial storage facilities use refrigeration or ventilation to hold temperatures below 30°F (-1°C) for long-term preservation.
claims.label: the below-30°F storage temperature

claims.text: Excessively high humidity promotes fungal growth, while low humidity can dry the grain out and cause it to shatter.
claims.label: humidity in both directions

claims.text: Air circulation is vital to prevent localized hot and cold spots and to distribute moisture evenly.
claims.label: air circulation through the store

claims.text: Regular cleaning and pest control are essential to prevent contamination by insects, rodents and microorganisms.
claims.label: cleaning and pest control
